Qal/Ni/Pi/Pu/Hithp: fill, be-full, accomplish (~252 occurrences spanning all OT). Standard concordant.
Aramaic; Dan 2:35; 3:19. Hyphenated.
Adjective from √male (fill); concordant 'full'. NL 'vol'.
From √male (be-full); that-which-fills a space or measure. NL 'volheid'.
From √male (fill); 'fillings of the hand', priest-installation offerings (Lev 8). Compound preserves the ceremonial 'fill-the-hand' kernel.
From √male (be-full). Harvest-fullness / firstfruits-bond (Ex 22:29; Num 18:27; Deu 22:9; Jer 2:3). Hyphenated for the firstfruits-context.
From √male (fill); jewel-setting in priestly garments (Ex 28:17,20; 39:13). Hyphenated for the technical compound.

Agent dispatched on a task; covers human envoys, prophets and the divine messenger ('angel'). KJV/ESV split into 'angel/messenger' contextually; the seven-anchor distribution shows one kernel of dispatch-function across all 212 occurrences. Greek angelos (LXX) preserves the same kernel.
Aramaic counterpart of H4397; Dan 3:28; 6:23. Hyphenated.
Substantive of malak-root; the activity-and-thing-made by the agent. Covers tabernacle workmanship (Ex 36), business (Gen 39:11), service. Concordant kernel 'work' across 166 occurrences.
Hapax (Hag 1:13). Abstract-noun from malak; the messenger-task. Hyphenated to bridge 'message' (the dispatched word) and 'business' (the work-aspect).
Proper-noun, prophet (Mal 1:1). Means 'my-messenger'. English convention: Malachi.
Hapax (Song 5:14). From √male; jewel-setting, contextually narrower than H4396.
From √labash (clothe); royal/festal apparel (1Ki 10:5; Zep 1:8; Eze 16:13). Hyphenated for the formal-occasion register; distinguished from beged H899 ('garment') and levush H3830 ('clothing').
From √laban (be-white) / leven (brick); brick-floor (2Sa 12:31; Jer 43:9; Nah 3:14). Hyphenated for the technical compound.
Late-Hebrew noun, mainly Job. Distinguished from H1697 davar by post-exilic literary register. Suffix '-II' marks lexical homonymy with the davar-domain.
Aramaic counterpart; Dan/Ezra. Hyphenated.
Place/structure-name, Jerusalem rampart (2Sa 5:9; 1Ki 9:15,24; 11:27; 2Ki 12:21; 2Chr 32:5). English convention: Millo.
Hapax (Job 30:4). Edible salt-plant. Standard botanical term.
Proper-noun, multiple persons. English convention: Malluch.
Family-name (Neh 12:14). MT-variant of H4409a. English convention.
Abstract-noun from malak (reign); the office and dignity of being-king. Distinguished from H4438 malkuth ('royalty', state) and H4467 mamlakah ('kingdom', realm). 24 occurrences.
From √lin (lodge); a place to spend the night (Gen 42:27; 43:21; Ex 4:24; Jos 4:3,8). Hyphenated for the place-noun sense.
From √lin (lodge); makeshift watch-shelter (Isa 1:8; 24:20). Hyphenated to capture both shelter and watchpost senses.
Proper-noun, son of Heman, 19th Levitical temple-singer division (1Chr 25:4,26). English convention: Mallothi.
Hapax (Isa 51:6) — heavens vanish like smoke. Hyphenated for the simile-bound sense; distinguished from homonym H4414b.
Homonym of H4414a (same consonants, different root). Salt-rubbing of newborns (Eze 16:4); seasoning of offerings (Lev 2:13). Hyphenated chain.
Aramaic idiom (Ezr 4:14): 'eat the salt of the palace' = be in the king's pay. Hyphenated.
Aramaic counterpart; salt as covenant-bond (Ezr 4:14; 6:9; 7:22). Hyphenated.
Standard. The mineral and its covenant-symbolism (Lev 2:13; Num 18:19; 2Chr 13:5; 2Ki 2:20-21). 28 occurrences.
Hapax-cluster (Jer 38:11,12). Worn-out garments, plural-form.
From √melach (salt); 'salt-man', sailor (Eze 27:9,27,29; Jon 1:5). Standard occupational term.
From √melach; barren saline waste (Job 39:6; Ps 107:34; Jer 17:6). Hyphenated.
From √lacham (fight). Concordant 'battle' across 319 occurrences. KJV/ESV use 'battle/war' interchangeably; 'battle' is the engagement-kernel; 'war' (broader campaign) surfaces as render-context.
Verb of slipping-away (Ni/Pi/Hi). 94 occurrences. KJV uses 'deliver/escape' contextually; 'escape' captures the kernel; causative 'cause-to-escape / deliver' surfaces in render.
Hapax (Jer 43:9). Lime-mortar binder for brick. Standard.
Proper-noun (Neh 3:7). Means 'YH delivers'. English convention.
Hapax (Deu 23:25). Plucked grain-ear. Hyphenated compound.
Used twice (Pro 1:6; Hab 2:6). Mocking-proverb / enigmatic-saying. Hyphenated to bridge 'satire' (Hab) and 'riddle' (Pro).

Verb 'be-king/reign'. 350 occurrences. KJV/ESV use 'reign/be-king/make-king' (Hi); 'reign' captures the kernel. Distinguished from mashal (rule, H4910), which has a broader 'rule-over' sense including non-royal authority.
Homonym of H4427a (Neh 5:7). Reflexive 'take counsel with oneself'. Hyphenated to mark the deliberative homonym.
Standard. 2519 occurrences — most-frequent royal noun in OT.
Proper-noun (1Chr 8:35; 9:41). Means 'king'. English convention.
Aramaic counterpart of melek; Ezr/Dan. 182 occurrences. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Dan 4:24). Aramaic 'counsel'. Hyphenated.
Ammonite deity to whom child-sacrifice was offered (Lev 18:21; 20:2-5; 1Ki 11:7; 2Ki 23:10; Jer 32:35). English convention: Molech. Etymologically related to H4445b Milcom.
Aramaic; queen-mother (Dan 5:10). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Job 18:10). Trap-noose. Hyphenated for the compound 'snare and trap'.
Proper-noun: wife of Nahor (Gen 11:29) and daughter of Zelophehad (Num 26:33; 27:1; 36:11; Jos 17:3). English convention: Milcah.
Feminine of melek; queen-consort or sovereign (Esth, 1Ki 10:1-13). 35 occurrences. Standard concordant 'queen'. Distinguished from H1377 gevirah ('great-lady') and H7694 shegal ('royal-consort').
Aramaic counterpart of mamlakah; Ezr/Dan. 54 occurrences. Hyphenated.

From malak; abstract 'royal state / dignity / reign'. 91 occurrences (esp. Esther, Daniel). Concordant kernel 'royalty' captures the dignity-state; KJV uses 'kingdom/royal estate' depending on context, which loses the abstraction. Distinguished from H4410 melukhah (kingship-as-office) and H4467 mamlakah (kingdom-as-realm).
Proper-noun, grandson of Asher (Gen 46:17; Num 26:45; 1Chr 7:31). Means 'my-king-is-El'. English convention.
Patronymic (Num 26:45). Standard suffix-form.
Proper-noun, multiple persons. Means 'my-king-is-YH'. English convention.
King of Salem, priest of El-Elyon (Gen 14:18; Ps 110:4). English convention: Melchizedek.
Variant entry (compound 'my-king-is-righteousness'). Same referent as H4442; standard transliteration kept.
Proper-noun, son of Jeconiah (1Chr 3:18). English convention.
Son of Saul (1Sa 14:49; 31:2; 1Chr 8:33; 9:39; 10:2). Means 'my-king-is-help'. English convention with hyphen.
Variant of H4444. Same referent.
Person (1Chr 8:9). English convention: Malcam.
Ammonite deity (1Ki 11:5,33; 2Ki 23:13; Jer 49:1,3; Zep 1:5). Distinguished from H4432 Molech though etymologically related; Milcom is the proper-noun form of the Ammonite chief deity.
Astral cult-figure (Jer 7:18; 44:17-25). Hyphenated compound preserves the title.
Proper-noun, woman of Manasseh (1Chr 7:18). English convention.
Verb 'speak' (poetic register; Pro 6:13; Job 8:2; 33:3; Ps 106:2). Hyphenated to mark this as the rare/emphatic 'speak' distinct from dabar (H1696, the standard 'speak').
Homonym of H4448a (Hapax, Job 14:2 — flower fades). Hyphenated for the wither-pole.
Aramaic; Dan 6:22; 7:11,20,25. Hyphenated.
Proper-noun (Neh 12:36). English convention.
Hapax (Jdg 3:31). Pointed driving-stick for oxen. Hyphenated compound.
Hapax (Ps 119:103). Hyphenated stative 'be-sweet'.
Persian loanword (Dan 1:11,16). Court-attendant/steward. Hyphenated to mark the loanword origin.
Used twice (Lev 1:15; 5:8) for the priestly bird-sacrifice technique. Hyphenated for the technical-act.
From √laqach (take); seized booty (Num 31:11ff; Isa 49:24-25). Hyphenated.
Homonym (Ps 22:16 [15]). The 'taking-place' of the mouth = palate.
Late-spring rain (Deu 11:14; Job 29:23; Pro 16:15; Jer 3:3; 5:24; Hos 6:3; Joe 2:23; Zec 10:1). Hyphenated standard agricultural term.
Dual form; lamp-trimming snuffers (Ex 25:38; 37:23; Num 4:9; 1Ki 7:49; 2Chr 4:21; Isa 6:6). Hyphenated.
Hapax (2Ki 10:22). Vestry/wardrobe-room for cult-garments.
Hapax (Job 29:17). The biting-teeth of the wicked. Hyphenated for compound.
Hapax (Joe 1:17). From √agar (gather). Hyphenated for compound.
Hapax (Job 38:5). From √madad (measure). Standard.
Persian counselor of Ahasuerus (Esth 1:14,16,21). English convention.
Plural-of-intensity from mavet (death); violent-deaths (Jer 16:4; Eze 28:8). Hyphenated to mark the plural-of-violence.

Used twice (Deu 23:3 [2]; Zec 9:6). Person of mixed/illegitimate descent. Transliteration retained because no English single-word covers the legal-cultic sense (KJV 'bastard' is too narrow / register-mismatched).
From √makar (sell); the act and object of sale (Lev 25:14,25-33,42,50; 1Ki 21:25; Neh 13:20; Eze 7:13). Hyphenated for the act-and-object compound.
Hapax (Lev 25:42). Specific to the prohibited selling-into-slavery. Hyphenated.

Concrete realm of a king. 116 occurrences. Concordant 'kingdom' for the territorial-political sense. Distinguished from H4438 malkuth (royalty/dignity), H4410 melukhah (kingship/office), H4468 mamlakhuth (royal-state, abstract).
Variant of mamlakah, more abstract (Jos 13:12,21,27,30,31; 1Sa 15:28; 2Sa 16:3; Jer 26:1; Hos 1:4). Hyphenated to distinguish from mamlakah.
Used twice (Pro 23:30; Isa 65:11). Spiced-wine mixture. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Pro 17:25). From √marar (be-bitter).
Place and person near Hebron (Gen 13:18; 14:13ff; 18:1; 23:17,19; 25:9; 35:27; 49:30; 50:13). English convention.
Hapax (Job 9:18). Intensification of marar; the cup-of-bitterness. Hyphenated for the saturation-sense.
Hapax (Eze 28:14). From √mashach (anoint); the anointed-spreading-cherub. Hyphenated.
From √mashal (rule); the area/extent of rule (Gen 1:16; 1Chr 26:6; Dan 11:3,5). Hyphenated for the rule-and-area compound.
Abstract-noun from √mashal; the act and right of ruling (Gen 1:16; 2Ki 20:13; Isa 22:21; Jer 34:1; Mic 4:8; Ps 114:2; 136:8-9). Hyphenated to bridge act and extent.
Hapax (Zep 2:9). 'Place of nettles'. Hyphenated.
Used twice (Neh 8:10; Song 5:16). Plural-of-intensity for sweetness.
The wilderness-bread (Ex 16; Num 11; Deu 8; Jos 5:12; Neh 9:20; Ps 78:24). Standard English convention.
Variant of H4478a; same referent. Marked separately in MT.
Aramaic interrogative pronoun; Dan/Ezra. Hyphenated.

Full-form ablative preposition; source/separation marker. 1221 occurrences. KJV uses 'from/of/out-of/since' depending on context; 'from' is the kernel. Distinguished from prefixed Hm (mi-, the proclitic short-form).
Variant entry (Ps 68:23 [22]). Same kernel as H4480a; the place-locked usage marked separately in MT.
Aramaic counterpart; 114 occurrences. Hyphenated.
From √manah (apportion); musical-string of stringed-instrument (Ps 45:9 [8]; 150:4). Hyphenated.
Aramaic verb; appoint, number, ordain (Dan 2:24,49; 3:12; 5:25-26). Hyphenated to bridge 'appoint' and 'number'.
Aramaic weight-unit; Dan 5:25-26 (the writing on the wall: MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Lam 3:63). From √nagan (play instrument); ironic song-of-mockery.
Aramaic; understanding/knowledge (Dan 2:21; 4:33,34 [36]; 5:12). Hyphenated.
Verb of counting/numbering/appointing (Gen 13:16; Num 23:10; 2Sa 24; 1Ki 8:5; Ps 90:12; Isa 53:12; Jon 1:17; 2:1; 4:6-8). 28 occurrences. Hyphenated to bridge counting and assigning.
Weight-unit (1Ki 10:17; Ezr 2:69; Eze 45:12). Standard English convention.
Used twice (Gen 31:7,41). 'Times' as in 'ten times'. Hyphenated for the count-instance sense.
From √manah (apportion); allotted share (1Sa 1:4-5; Neh 8:10,12; Ps 11:6; 16:5; 63:11; Est 2:9; 9:19,22). 14 occurrences. Standard concordant.
Hapax (2Ki 9:20). The way of driving (Jehu's chariot). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Jdg 6:2). Mountain-shelter/den. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Ps 44:14). From √nud (shake/wander). Hyphenated.
From √nuach (rest); place of rest (Gen 8:9; Deu 28:65; Isa 34:14; Lam 1:3; Mic 2:10; Ru 3:1; Ps 116:7). Hyphenated.
Father of Samson (Jdg 13). Means 'rest'. English convention.

Feminine of manoach; the rest-state and rest-location (Gen 49:15; Num 10:33; Deu 12:9; Jdg 20:43; 1Ki 8:56; Isa 11:10; Mic 2:10; Ps 23:2; 95:11; 132:8,14). 22 occurrences. Hyphenated to bridge state and place.
Hapax (Pro 29:21). Disputed: heir / insolent / continuator. Concordant 'insolence' follows the disrespect-pole (TWOT).
From √nus (flee); place-of-flight, refuge (Job 11:20; Ps 142:5; Jer 16:19; 25:35; Am 2:14). Hyphenated.
Used twice (Lev 26:36; Isa 52:12). Act of flight.
Large beam of the loom (Jdg 16:14; 1Sa 17:7; 2Sa 21:19; 1Chr 11:23; 20:5). Hyphenated.
From √nur/ner (lamp). Standard concordant 'lampstand' across 42 occurrences (tabernacle/temple).
Hapax (Nah 3:17). 'Crowned/chosen ones'. Hyphenated to mark the elite-troops sense.
Cereal/tribute offering. KJV 'meat-offering' (archaic 'meat'='food'); NIV/ESV 'grain-offering'. The kernel is the non-blood offering (Lev 2; 6:14-23). Hyphenated technical term. 211 occurrences.
Aramaic counterpart; Ezr 7:17; Dan 2:46. Hyphenated.
King of Israel (2Ki 15:14-22). Means 'comforter'. English convention.
Place (1Chr 8:6). Hyphenated disambiguator from H4506b.
Person (Gen 36:23; 1Chr 1:40). English convention.
Hapax (Isa 65:11). Babylonian-Persian fortune-deity. Hyphenated disambiguator.
Hapax (Jer 51:27). Region near Ararat. English convention.
Multiple persons (1Chr 24:9; Ezr 10:25; Neh 10:7; 12:5,17,41). English convention.
Hapax (Ezr 6:17). Aramaic 'number'. Hyphenated.
Ammonite location (Jdg 11:33; Eze 27:17). English convention.
Hapax (Job 15:29). Acquired wealth. Hyphenated.
Verb of withholding/refusing (Gen 30:2; Num 24:11; Job 22:7; Ps 84:12; Pro 1:11; 3:27; 11:26; 23:13; 30:7; etc.). 29 occurrences. Standard concordant.
From √naal (bolt); door-lock (Song 5:5; Neh 3:3,6,13-15). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Deu 33:25). 'Your bolt iron and brass'. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Neh 8:10). Sweet foods.
Hapax (2Sa 6:5). Percussion-shaker. Hyphenated.
From √nakah (clean) — pure-bowl for drink-offerings (Ex 25:29; 37:16; Num 4:7; Jer 52:19). Hyphenated.
Son of Joseph; tribe; multiple kings (146 occurrences). English convention.
Patronymic (Deu 4:43; Jdg 12:4; 2Ki 10:33). Standard suffix-form.
Variant of manah (H4490); allotted share (Neh 12:44,47; 13:10; Jer 13:25; Ps 11:6; 16:5; 63:11). Hyphenated.
Corvée/conscript-labor (Gen 49:15; Ex 1:11; Deu 20:11; Jos 16:10; Jdg 1:28-35; 1Ki 4:6; 5:13-14; 9:15,21; etc.). 22 occurrences. Hyphenated technical term.
Hapax (Job 6:14). The melting-of-heart, despondent person. Distinguished from H4522 by stem and context.
Used (Song 1:12; 1Sa 16:11; 2Ki 23:5). The reclining-couch around a table. Hyphenated.
From √sagar (close); the metal-worker who closes/locks (2Ki 24:14,16; Jer 24:1; 29:2; Ps 142:8). Hyphenated.
Architectural border (Ex 25:25-27; 37:12-14; 1Ki 7:28-36; 2Ki 16:17). Hyphenated.
Hapax (1Ki 7:9). Foundation-stones. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Jdg 3:23). Vestibule-corridor. Hyphenated.
Verb of melting (Ps 6:7 [6]; 39:12 [11]; 147:18). Hyphenated to bridge physical and metaphorical melting.
Hapax (Deu 16:10). Free-will offering measured by hand. Hyphenated.
From √nasah (test); the testing-event (Deu 4:34; 7:19; 29:3 [2]). Hyphenated.
Variant; the act/state of being-tested (Deu 6:16; 9:22; 33:8; Ps 95:8; Job 9:23). Hyphenated.
Wilderness location (Ex 17:7; Deu 6:16; 9:22; 33:8). Means 'testing'. Hyphenated for the place-noun marker.
Used (Ex 34:33,34,35). The face-veil of Moses. Standard.
Hapax (Mic 7:4). From √suk (hedge). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Isa 22:8). Defensive shield/post.
Hapax (Isa 5:7). Disputed; concordant 'tally/count' from sephar-sister-root.
Verb of mixing wine (Pro 9:2,5; Isa 5:22; 19:14; Ps 102:10 [9]). Hyphenated for the technical wine-mixing sense.
Hapax (Ps 75:9 [8]). From √masak. Standard.
The curtain-screen of the tabernacle (Ex 26:36-37; 27:16; 35:12; 36:37; etc.). 25 occurrences. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Eze 28:13). Setting/covering of jewels. Hyphenated.
From √nasak (pour); cast-metal idol (Ex 32:4,8; 34:17; Lev 19:4; Deu 9:12; 27:15; etc.). 27 occurrences. Hyphenated.
Homonym (Isa 25:7; 28:20; 30:1,22). The covering-veil. Hyphenated.
Adjective; the social-class poor (Ecc 4:13; 9:15-16). Hyphenated to capture both poverty and clientship.
Storage-city plural (Ex 1:11; 1Ki 9:19; 2Chr 8:4-6; 16:4; 17:12; 32:28). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Deu 8:9). Lack/scarcity. Hyphenated.
Used twice (Jdg 16:13,14). The loom-frame and warp-threads. Hyphenated.
Built-up road/causeway (Num 20:19; Jdg 20:31-32; 21:19; 1Sa 6:12; 2Ki 18:17; etc.). 27 occurrences. Standard.
Hapax (Isa 35:8). Variant of mesillah; same English equivalent.
Standard. Iron/wooden nail (1Chr 22:3; 2Chr 3:9; Isa 41:7; Jer 10:4; Ecc 12:11).
Verb of melting/weakening (Ex 16:21; Deu 1:28; 20:8; Jos 2:9-11; 5:1; 7:5; 14:8; etc.). 22 occurrences. Hyphenated to capture the away-aspect (cessation in fear).
From √nasa (pull-up tent-stakes); a single travel-stage (Gen 13:3; Ex 17:1; 40:36-38; Num 10:6,12,28; 33:1-2; Deu 10:11). 12 occurrences. Hyphenated.
Hapax (1Ki 6:7). The quarry-cutting site. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Job 41:18 [26]). Throwing-spear. Standard.
Hapax (2Ki 18:16). Support/leaning-place. Standard.
Funeral-wail (Gen 50:10; Deu 26:14; Isa 22:12; Jer 6:26; Eze 24:17; etc.). 14 occurrences. Hyphenated.
Animal-feed (Gen 24:25,32; 42:27; 43:24; Jdg 19:19). Hyphenated.
Used twice (Eze 13:18,21). Magical wrap. Hyphenated.
Skin-eruption diagnosis (Lev 13:6-8; 14:56). Hyphenated.
Standard. From √safar (count). 133 occurrences.
Hapax (Ezr 2:2). Person-name. English convention.
Variant of H4558 (Neh 7:7). English convention.
Used twice (Num 31:5,16). Levy/deliver-up. Hyphenated for the deliver-action.
Hapax (Job 33:16). Variant of musar; the disciplining-bond. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Eze 20:37). 'I will bring you into the bond of the covenant'. Hyphenated.
Hapax (Isa 4:6). Hiding-place. Standard.
Hapax (Isa 53:3). 'As one from whom men hide their faces'. Hyphenated.
From √sathar (hide); secret-corner (Ps 10:9; 17:12; 64:5 [4]; 81:8 [7]; Isa 45:3; Jer 13:17; 23:24; 49:10; Lam 3:10; Hab 3:14). Hyphenated.
Hapax (Job 34:25). Plural of paal-noun; works-of-evil. Hyphenated to capture the negative-context.
Hapax (Dan 4:2 [3]). 'Signs and wonders' — the JHWH-works. Aramaic with hyphen.
Hapax (Ps 69:3 [2]). 'I sink in deep mire and there is no maamad'. The (lacking) standing-place in clay-bottom. Hyphenated.
From √abar (pass); river-ford / mountain-pass (Gen 32:23 [22]; 1Sa 14:4). Hyphenated.
Variant; broader passage-locations (Isa 30:32; Jdg 3:28; Jos 2:7; Isa 10:29; etc.). Hyphenated.
